title: Endpoint Detection Engineering | Splunk, Sysmon, MITRE ATT&CK
description: Built a Windows endpoint detection environment using Splunk and Sysmon to simulate, detect, and investigate four MITRE ATT&CK techniques: LSASS Credential Dumping (T1003.001), Malicious Service Creation (T1543.003), Registry Run Key Persistence (T1547.001), and Scheduled Task Persistence (T1053.005). Authored SPL detection rules with automated alerting, tuned to zero false positives. All findings documented in structured incident reports, detection logic write-ups, and portfolio case studies following SOC documentation standards.

title: LSASS Credential Dumping: Detection & Investigation | Microsoft Defender, KQL
description: Emulated a realistic LSASS credential-theft attack chain against a Microsoft Defender for Endpoint monitored Windows Server, then ran a full blue-team investigation to validate detection coverage. Used KQL advanced hunting across process, file, and network telemetry to reconstruct the attack lifecycle from a PowerShell download cradle through credential dumping (T1003.001) to post-exploitation discovery, enriched findings with VirusTotal threat intelligence, and confirmed impact through on-disk artifact analysis. Authored reusable KQL detection analytics with false-positive tuning and documented the investigation in a structured incident report following SOC documentation standards.
